1) the β-catenin and c-jun genes are transcriptional targets for each other; 2) the c-jun and β-catenintarget genes are transcriptionally activated by the JNK/c-Jun pathway; and 3) the β-catennin and JNK signaling pathways cooperate to regulate cell proliferation, differentiation, migration, and apoptosis.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcriptional and signaling mechanisms that regulate cell proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, and carcinogenesis.
the role of the transcription factors β-catenin and c-Jun and their signaling partners JNK and TCF4 in cancer.
how transcriptional regulation is linked to the β-catenin and JNK signaling pathways, how these pathways interact with one another, and their role in carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
β-catenins and JNKs are important in the development of many different cancers and that they are important in the maintenance of normal cells.

the β-catenin and JNK signaling pathways are intimately linked, and that their cooperation may contribute to the development of human cancer.

c-jun is a common target of β-catenin and JNK signaling pathways.
β-catenins and c-JUN are important transcription factors that regulate the expression of genes that are critical to the development of the embryo, the adult, and cancer.
